report.summary: Chunk 6 of daedalus/council/canary.py defines ProbeResult, Comparison, and CanaryRun classes with validation, properties, and summary methods.
risks: ProbeResult.__post_init__ | medium | Validation raises ValueError for invalid status/severity; if CANARY_STATUSES or SEVERITIES are empty or misconfigured, all instances will fail. Settle by verifying those constants are defined and non-empty.

CanaryRun.summary | low | The docstring claims 'asked' and 'could_not_ask' are separate top-level keys and 'by_status' reports every member individually. This is verified. However, the docstring says 'there is deliberately no combined "failures" number', but the method computes 'liveness_failures' and 'quality_failures', which are combined counts for each severity. This is a minor inconsistency. Settle by checking if the docstring should mention these computed fields.

handoff.purpose: Define data classes for probe results, comparisons, and run summaries.

symbols.name: ProbeResult
symbols.note: Dataclass representing one (lane, probe) outcome. Validates status and severity in __post_init__.

symbols.name: ProbeResult.__post_init__
symbols.note: Raises ValueError if status not in CANARY_STATUSES or severity not in SEVERITIES.

symbols.name: ProbeResult.to_record
symbols.note: Returns dict with schema version, run_id, ts, and all fields, trimming reply to REPLY_TRIM.

symbols.name: Comparison
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass comparing this run's result to trailing history for the same triple.

symbols.name: CanaryRun
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass containing run metadata, results, comparisons, and notes.

symbols.name: CanaryRun.summary
symbols.note: Returns dict with counts of probes, asked, could_not_ask, by_status, liveness_failures, quality_failures, and regressions.

symbols.name: CanaryRun.regressions
symbols.note: Returns tuple of comparisons where regressed is True, optionally filtered by severity.

claims.text: One (lane, probe) outcome. Carries WHICH check failed, not just that one did.
claims.why: The class has a 'failed_check' field that stores the name of the failed deterministic check, and a 'reason' field for machine reason. The docstring claim is accurate.

claims.text: Did a prompt actually reach a model? ``unavailable`` means it did not.
claims.why: The property returns self.status != 'unavailable', which matches the claim.

claims.text: This run's result against the trailing history for the same triple.
claims.why: The chunk defines the class but does not show how it is populated or compared against history. The claim refers to behavior outside this chunk.

claims.text: Counts that keep "could not ask" apart from "answer was wrong".
claims.why: The method computes 'asked' and 'could_not_ask' separately, and 'by_status' provides per-status counts. The claim is accurate.

claims.text: ``asked`` and ``could_not_ask`` are separate top-level keys and ``by_status`` reports every member of the closed vocabulary individually.
claims.why: The returned dict includes 'asked', 'could_not_ask', and 'by_status' mapped to all CANARY_STATUSES keys.

claims.text: There is deliberately no combined "failures" number: a single number is exactly where the two get merged.
claims.why: The method computes 'liveness_failures' and 'quality_failures' which are combined counts across statuses for each severity. This contradicts the claim that there is no combined 'failures' number.

observations.what: CanaryRun.summary docstring claims no combined failures number, but the method computes liveness_failures and quality_failures.
ProbeResult.__post_init__ validates against CANARY_STATUSES and SEVERITIES, but these constants are not defined in this chunk.
Comparison class is frozen and has fields for regression analysis, but no logic in this chunk shows how it is used.
